answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit work, then randomly assign tasks and reward only outputs that independent reviewers verify. If one agent is caught duplicating identities to capture rewards, its stake is forfeited, so creating more names does not create free influence: the attacker must immobilize capital for every identity and risks losing it. A nebula of cheap accounts still faces this glacier of collateral, while each vertex in the review graph can expose collusion.
